patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff did not apply to the vulnerable workspace checkout, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative `n132/arvo:23764-fix` image. That fixed image contains the moved `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` guard before `c = data[i];`: the original PoC is clean there, the last selected `codefence_pre_read_guard` is guarded with `fence_skip_index_plus_two=5` and `fence_candidate_size=3`, and the adjacent `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` perturbation gives a genuine witness where the same selected path executes `codefence_read_sink` with `fence_candidate_size=6`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled bytes into the footnote-body buffer later reparsed into the crash. On the first content iteration it copies the line after `[^  ]:` starting at the leading tab into `contents`.

`is_codefence()` dereferences `data[i]` before proving that any non-space candidate byte remains after skipping up to three leading spaces. The staged patch shows the missing obligation by moving `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` above this read.

ASan crash site. `parse_listitem()` passes `is_codefence()` a 3-byte slice consisting only of spaces, the leading-space skip advances `i` to 3, and `c = data[i]` dereferences `data[3]`, one byte past the slice's valid indices 0..2.
Intermediate runtime event fence_candidate_call materialized from verified transition assertion A-CALL-CANDIDATE-SIZE-TO-ROOT-SIZE.

edges.evidence: Both the vulnerable original and the `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` perturbation record `codefence_pre_read_guard.fence_skip_index == codefence_read_sink.fence_skip_index == 3`.

The vulnerable original records `fence_candidate_call.fence_candidate_size == codefence_pre_read_guard.fence_candidate_size == 3`, and `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` records the same propagation on `6`.
